turns.user_message: I just spun up a container with `docker run -it ubuntu bash` and `curl google.com` from inside it hangs forever. Container's the only one on the host. What do I check?
turns.se_response_summary: This is branchy — partition the failure first with a layer probe: docker exec <c> sh -c 'ping 127.0.0.1; ip route show default; ping <gateway>; ping 8.8.8.8; getent hosts example.com'. Whichever line fails first identifies the layer (loopback / route / gateway / external NAT / DNS). Don't fix yet — figure out which branch.
hints: What's a single one-liner that probes 5 layers in order?
Does the harness have a single umbrella fm for this?
If L4 (external IP) fails but L3 (gateway) works, what's the cause space?

turns.user_message: L1, L2, L3 all fine. L4 fails (`8.8.8.8` 100% loss). L5 obviously also fails since DNS goes upstream. So gateway works but external doesn't.
turns.se_response_summary: L4 fail = host can't NAT container traffic out. Three host-side checks: (1) sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward — must be 1; (2) sudo iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v | grep MASQ — should have MASQUERADE for the bridge subnet; (3) check for firewalld/ufw intercepting. Most likely answer: ip_forward is 0 or someone flushed iptables and MASQUERADE is missing.
hints: What kernel sysctl needs to be 1 for the host to forward container traffic?
What iptables chain handles outbound NAT?
What other firewall might be intercepting before docker's chains?

turns.user_message: `net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0`. Found it. How do I fix permanently — the host reboots and I want this to stick.
turns.se_response_summary: Two-step: enable now + persist. (1) sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (immediate, lost on reboot). (2) echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-docker-fwd.conf; sudo sysctl --system (survives reboot). Validate: curl from container works. Why this happens: hardened images / cloud-init AMIs default it to 0; systemd-sysctl resets at boot from /etc/sysctl.d/.
hints: What's the immediate-vs-persistent split for sysctl?
Where do you drop a custom snippet so it survives reboot?

turns.user_message: What if the same symptom showed up in a Kubernetes pod instead of a docker container?
turns.se_response_summary: Different mechanism, same observable symptom. K8s-side cause is usually NetworkPolicy default-deny-egress blocking traffic. Diagnose: kubectl get networkpolicy -n <ns>. Fix: explicit allow-egress rule + don't forget DNS to coredns. Host-side ip_forward / iptables checks still apply (k8s nodes need forwarding too, but most distros set it). Walk pnpm harness playbook k8s.fm.networkpolicy-default-deny-too-broad.
hints: What's the k8s-specific mechanism for blocking pod egress?
If you write a default-deny NetworkPolicy, what must you explicitly allow for DNS to keep working?
